WDH

WDH is a multidisciplinary team of builders, coders, and space enthusiasts competing in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Using open-source NASA and partner space agency datasets, we design practical software, data visualizations, and scalable prototypes aimed at solving real-world challenges on Earth and supporting humanity's journey to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
summary:
**SPHERSUB – Revealing Astronomical Changes Through Image Subtraction**

SPHERSUB is an accessible astronomical image-comparison platform designed to identify changes between two observations of the same region of space.

Users upload two images (Epoch 1 and Epoch 2). The platform aligns the images, subtracts matching stationary features, and makes moving or changed features easier to identify. A 10-zone scan then examines the resulting image across ten separate regions.

SPHERSUB has been tested with more than 2,000 different images, including extremely crowded starfields. It aims to make astronomical image analysis easier and more accessible, even for people without a scientific background.

The platform requires no registration, login, or account, allowing anyone to access it.

Its potential applications include identifying moving astronomical objects, highlighting changes between observations, and supporting certain astronomical investigations, including exoplanet direct-imaging research.

**Live Website:** https://pulkitwdh.github.io/SpherSub/

**GitHub Repository:** https://github.com/PulkitWDH/SpherSub.git
